chapters.title: All My Love
chapters.html:
Phainon was supposed to be alone.

He’d made sure of that. Mydei was working downstairs in the bakery and Augusta was busy having a tea party with her ever-growing collection of toys. He figured he had around ten minutes to himself, maybe fifteen if he was lucky. 

The little velvet box sat closed on the bed behind him. He stood in front of the closet, fingers drumming against his side as he contemplated what he could move and where the best hiding spot would be. 

He thought about putting it in a box of old costumes but Augusta had been rummaging through it lately for her dress-up games, so the possibility of Mydei finding the ring wasn’t exactly zero. He glanced back at the box, picking up. Phainon held it in his hand, heart thudding against his chest despite himself. 

He shouldn’t have been nervous. He was sure Mydei had been dropping hints of wanting a ring, and they were practically already married between shared routines and spending time with their daughter. Still, the possibility of messing things up completely crept into the corners of his mind. 

He pushed the thoughts aside, smiling faintly as he opened the box. 

The ring was simple and elegant—something he thought Mydei would like. Something that would catch the light when Mydei lifted his hand to tuck his hair behind his ear or pick up a cup of coffee.  

Maybe he could hide it by the winter-wear? They wouldn’t be taking any of that stuff out anytime soon. 

Phainon let out a little groan. That wouldn’t work either. His ever-busy partner had been on a spring cleaning kick lately and he still hadn’t gone through their closet yet.

“Papa, what are you doing?”

Phainon startled, hiding his hands behind his back as he looked over at Augusta in the doorway. She was half-hidden behind the doorframe, one of her stuffed animals tucked under one arm and the other hand on her hip. 

“Nothing,” he said, a little too quickly. “Just looking through some… books.”

Augusta furrowed her brows, looking around the room, clearly puzzled. “But there aren’t any books.”

“No. Well. Technically, no,” he muttered, running his free hand through his hair. “But you didn’t see anything.”

“Is it for Mama?”

Phainon opened his mouth, paused, then sighed. “Maybe.”

Her expression shifted, more curious than suspicious now.

“Is it a secret?” she asked, lowering her voice to a hushed whisper. 

Phainon knelt down in front of her, eyes wide. “Yes. A very big one, and it’s very important. Which means…” he held up a finger. “You can’t tell. Or auntie Cipher and Cas. Not even grandma and grandpa.”

Augusta nodded along to his words, eyes wide as she hugged Fig Stew closer. “...Are you and Mama going to get married?” 

Phainon smiled and nodded. “That’s the plan,” he winked. 

“Okay! I promise I won’t tell anyone,” she nodded solemnly, clearly trying to contain her excitement, but she was already bouncing on her heels.

Phainon shook his head fondly, making his way over to the linen closet in the hall instead with Augusta on his trail. Maybe he’d have better luck there instead. 

“Papa.”

“Mhm?”

“You can’t hide it there!”

Phainon blinked. “Oh?”

She nodded, reaching out to tug on his sleeve until she rounded the corner to her own bedroom. She crouched down near the foot of her bed, seemingly rummaging through a few things before pulling out a pink box covered in glitter glue and stickers. She turned to him with a grin. 

“You can put it in here! Mama never looks inside,” she began, “he hates when he gets glitter on his hands.”

Phainon chuckled, tucking the velvet box inside before pulling Augusta into his lap. “What would I—mwah—” he pressed an exaggerated kiss to her cheek as she giggled. “—do without you?”

She giggled again when he pressed another kiss against her cheek just as footsteps padded across the floor. Mydei appeared in the doorway, eyes soft, crossing his arms over his chest as he leaned against the doorframe. 

God, was he pretty. Even tired, with a few loose strands of hair framing his face and smear of flour on his sleeve, he was still radiant. 

“What are you two up to?” he asked. 

“Papa—”

Phainon clapped a hand over Augusta’s mouth before she could dig them into a hole he wasn’t sure he’d be able to lie his way out of. She let out a small squeak, and Mydei raised an eyebrow but didn’t question further. Phainon stood with her in his arms, gently kicking the pink box back under the bed before crossing the room over to Mydei. 

He reached out to brush a smudge of flour off of Mydei’s cheek before leaning in to press a gentle kiss against the spot. 

“Just waiting on you.”

☼

Phainon adjusted the collar of his shirt for the fifth time. He was standing outside of Mydei’s childhood home with a box of pastries in one hand and a modest bouquet of flowers in the other. Just a few sunflowers, some sprigs of lavender, and a few white blossoms. 

He’d gotten up early to make the pastries, leaving a few of them at home for Augusta and Mydei when they woke up. It was a handwritten recipe his mother had sent him a couple of years back when he’d left, so he could have a taste of home wherever he went. 

He took a deep breath before raising a hand to knock. He knew that he had no reason to be nervous. He and Mydei had been together for some time now and they were already sharing a life together. 

But still, the sinking feeling in his stomach wouldn’t rest. Gorgo and Eurypon meant a lot to Mydei. They had always been present when Phainon hadn’t been. 

The front door swung open, pulling him out of his spiral. Gorgo stood on the other side, and Phainon could’ve sworn her eyes softened at the sight of him. 

“Phainon, what a nice surprise,” she said warmly, taking in the items in his hands, and his slightly panicked expression. 

“I hope I’m not interrupting anything,” he managed, offering her a sheepish smile. “I–I brought breakfast, it’s one of my mother’s recipes. And these,” he added, holding up the flowers. 

Gorgo stepped aside to let him in, her eyes shining. “Any morning that starts with fresh pastries and flowers is hardly an interruption, my dear. Come in, come in. Eurypon’s in the sitting room.”

He toed off his shoes by the door as Gorgo reached out and gently took the item from his hands. “These are beautiful. Now, how is Mydei? And the little one? We don’t see you three often.”

“Just a little…busy,” Phainon replied with a small laugh. “Mydei’s been preparing for the holiday rush and Augusta has a lot more energy than either of us know what to do with.”

Gorgo gave a small huff in response, setting the pastries down on the kitchen counter. They stepped into the sitting room where Eurypon was flipping through a book. He looked up at the sound of footsteps and blinked. 

“Phainon,” he said, pleasantly surprised. “Mydei isn’t with you?”

“No, sir,” Phainon responded. 

Eurypon raised an eyebrow at the formality. “Oh?”

Phainon offered a tentative smile, his hands already beginning to fidget with the hem of his sleeve. “There’s actually something I’ve been wanting to ask the two of you,” he said, looking between the older couple. 

They shared a look, comfortable silence settling between them. Eurypon set his book down as Gorgo set a few pastries on a plate to bring them over to the table. 

“Of course, darling,” she said, easing into her seat beside her husband. 

Phainon took the seat across from them. “I don’t exactly know how to say this to be completely honest,” he laughed lightly. “I didn’t think I’d be this nervous, but Mydei and I—”

“No,” Eurypon cut in. 

Phainon blinked and Gorgo shook her head, shooting her husband a glare. 

Eurypon cleared his throat. “My apologies. Force of habit. Please continue.”

“Mydei and I have been together for quite some time now, and I know I wasn’t there when August was born,” he frowned slightly. “ —but I’m here now, and I love your son, and I think you’ve known that longer than I have. You’ve been there for him through it all, and I know he’d want your approval—so I’m here to ask for your blessing to marry Mydei.”

There was a beat of silence. 

Eurypon leaned back slightly in his chair, eyes narrowing in thought. Gorgo’s expression had already softened as she reached over to touch her husband’s arm. 

Phainon held their gaze, fingers tightening slightly where they rested on his knees. He’d tried not to ramble. There were billions of things he could’ve said about Mydei and why he wanted to marry him, but he waited. 

Eurypon was the first to break the silence. “I always imagined I’d have more time to prepare for this talk.”

“Please,” Gorgo playfully rolled her eyes. “You’ve had more than five years.”

“And they went by like nothing.”

She shook her head, smiling faintly. “When we first met you back then, I never thought we’d ended up here because well—” she gestured vaguely and Phainon wasn’t sure if he should take it as a compliment or an insult. “ —but you have our blessing. You’ve always had it and even if you didn’t, Mydei, he loves you and that’s enough.”

Phainon exhaled, leaning forward slightly. “Thank you. Really.”

Eurypon patted his hand with a fond smile. “Now, don’t keep us waiting too long. We’ll be expecting those wedding invites soon.”

“I’ll try my best.”

☼

The scent of rain clung to the aid, the pavement damp and glistening under their boots. Phainon held onto Augusta’s hand as they walked, her little rain boots splashing confidently through shallow puddles despite his gentle attempts to steer her away from them. 

She tugged on his arm, hopping into another puddle. “Did you ask Mama yet?”

Phainon sighed, albeit fondly. “What did we say about talking about that, hm?”

Augusta groaned. “Not to,” she muttered, head tilting up to look at him. “But Mama isn’t even here!” she added. “He won’t hear us.”

Phainon stifled a laugh, catching her other hand to lift her up before she could veer into another puddle. “It’s still a secret, babygirl. Even if Mama isn’t here.”

She huffed, looking at him with pleading eyes. “But I want to be a flower girl again. Last time was so fun!”

“And you will be,” he reassured her, gently tugging the hood of her raincoat back up and patting her head.

“Promise?”

“Promise,” he nodded, grinning as he leaned in to kiss her cheek. He pulled back to look at her, playfully narrowing his eyes and poking a finger to her stomach. “As long as you don’t spoil the surprise.”

“I won’t,” she said solemnly, her expression so serious it made him laugh. 

☼

It was quiet, the kind of warm evening that came after the day had softened. Dinner had been lively and with the weeks going by, Phainon was becoming increasingly worried that Augusta would accidentally mention something over dinner. He couldn’t blame her either. She was excited, and he was the one holding off on asking. 

He just wanted it to be perfect. Mydei deserved that. 

Phainon sat curled up in his usual corner, phone in hand as he idly scrolled without much purpose. He just needed something to do with his hands. 

He heard Mydei padding across the floor but didn’t look up until the cushions shifted and the weight of a familiar body settled into his lap, one leg sliding over his thigh, followed by the other. Mydei’s robe had fallen open slightly, and he was straddling him, cool fingers pressing lightly to Phainon’s chest. 

“Oh,” Phainon said, looking up at him. “Hi.”

“Hi,” Mydei murmured, but didn’t give him time to say anything more. He leaned in and kissed the curve of Phainon’s neck in the slow and deliberate way he knew Phainon loved, lips brushing beneath his ear before drifting down to his jaw. His hands smoothed under the hem of Phainon’s shirt, palms resting against his stomach. “You’ve been off lately.”

“Off?” Phainon tilted his head, letting his phone fall to the cushions and loosely resting his hand on Mydei’s bare thigh. “How so?”

Mydei hummed against his skin. “You’re not as clingy anymore.”

“Me? Clingy?” Phainon echoed. 

Mydei just pulled back slightly, narrowing his eyes at him. “You used to kiss me every chance you got. Now you just sit here.”

Phainon laughed, wrapping his arms around Mydei’s waist. “Sounds like someone is needy,” he teased. 

“Don’t deflect,” Mydei responded. “If you’re cheating on me—”

“Cheating?!” Phainon interrupted, a little too loudly but caught himself. 

“You’ve been all secretive lately. Sneaking out, making pastries, and buying flowers a few weeks ago that you never gave to me,” Mydei listed off. “I saw that charge on your card.”

“That–that wasn’t—” Phainon sputtered, but he took a breath, straightening a little as he reached up to cup Mydei’s face in his hands. “I would never in a million years cheat on you. There’s no reality where that would happen.”

“Then what’s gotten you acting so cagey, hm?”

Phainon smirked. “Wouldn’t you like to know.” Then, without warning, he shifted his grip and pushed forward, catching Mydei off balance. Mydei let out a small surprised sound as he was pinned to the couch, back sinking into the cushions as Phainon hovered over him. 

“Phai—”

“Mm,” Phainon murmured, leaning down to brush his lips across the other man’s jaw. “I guess I’ve been slacking. Should I make it up to you?”

“I know–ah—” Mydei breathed, voice already shifting into something lower and needier. “ —what you’re doing.”

“Do you?” Phainon asked, and kissed him until Mydei forgot what he was about to say. 

☼

The room was quiet save for the faint rustle of sheets and the faint sound of dishes clanking from the kitchen. Phainon was sitting on the edge of Augusta’s bed, one hand smoothing over her blanket. 

She was already halfway asleep, and it was the kind of peacefulness that always made something in his chest ache with tenderness. He leaned in, brushing a gentle kiss against her forehead. “Night, sweetheart.”

Papaaa,” her eyes blinked open. “Did you change your mind?”

“What?”

“About asking Mama,” she whispered. 

“No, babygirl,” he murmured, brushing some of her hair away from her eyes. “I didn’t change my mind. You won’t have to keep the secret anymore soon,” he added as he tapped her nose. 

She giggled at that, eyes dropping from sleep. Her lashes fluttered gently as she opened her mouth to speak. “I can’t wait for the...” her little voice trailed off.

Her eyes were already closed now as she drifted off, the words lingering between them. Phainon smiled at that. 

Then the floor creaked. 

Phainon’s head whipped around, only to find Mydei leaning against the doorframe, arms crossed loosely over his chest. His voice was quiet. “For the what?”

Phainon’s heart skipped a beat, afraid that Mydei might’ve overhead more than he’d anticipated. “Hm?”

Mydei tilted his head. “What were you two talking about?”

Phainon shrugged, standing carefully as to not wake her. “The park. She’s just excited to play tomorrow.”

Mydei didn’t say anything. Just watched him with a knowing sort of amusement as Phainon moved past him into the hall. 

“Very convincing,” Mydei murmured as he closed the door. “You’re a bad liar.”

Mydei threw an arm around his shoulders as Phainon exhaled through his nose. 

“I’ll figure out what you two are plotting,” he said, kissing his cheek. 

Not if Phainon could help it. 

☼

“You said we were just going for a walk,” Mydei said, glancing around. 

The sun had just begun to dip below the horizon and the early evening light painted the city in streaks of gold and purple. They were heading down the sidewalk, Phainon had one hand in Mydei’s and the other in his coat pocket, toying with the velvet box. 

“We are. This is a walk.”

“Your hand is clammy.”

Phainon pouted. “You hand is warm.”

Mydei playfully rolled his eyes, hooking their arms together instead just as they approached their destination. 

Phainon had contemplated for longer than he wanted to admit. His mind kept circling the options of how, where, and when he’d propose to Mydei. He wanted it to be perfect. 

That’s how he’d settled on the little cobblestone path near the bistro where it all happened. Little lights strung across the front glimmered lightly as patrons walked in and out. The air was cool but not chilly. It was almost like that day. 

The day Phainon had run into Mydei and Castorice. He remembered it like yesterday. It hadn’t been long since he’d returned to the city and he’d spent nights agonizing over whether reconnecting with Mydei after everything would be selfish or cruel. But then, he’d seen him and every bit of resolve had crumbled in that moment. 

Phainon smiled at the memory, taking both of Mydei’s hands, not missing the smile tugging at the other man’s lips. 

“Do you remember this place?”

“Like I’d forget,” Mydei titled his head slightly. “I was…mortified when I saw you here.”

“Let’s go with ecstatic or thrilled.”

“Mm, sure,” Mydei huffed a small laugh, turning away toward the entrance, but Phainon pulled him back in with ease. Mydei raised an eyebrow. “Are we going in?”

“The day—” Phainon’s voice caught in his throat. He;d barely gotten the words out and tears already pricked at the corners of his eyes. He didn’t trust himself to speak without tears falling. Mydei’s hand moved up to cup his cheek. 

“Hey… what is it?” he asked gently. 

Phainon shook his head, closing his eyes for a moment. “That day when I saw you again and you were with Cas, I thought ‘this is it, this is my chance to make things right’ but then you looked troubled and I—I thought I really blew it.”

“I was still trying to figure out how to tell you about Augusta, it was never your fault,” Mydei responded gently, his voice apologetic. 

Phainon took the hand cupping his cheek, intertwining their fingers. “No, no that’s not—God, I’m really messing this up,” he ran one hand over his face. “What I mean to say is that—I got so much more than I could ever ask for and I feel we’ve been doing things backwards. Raising Augusta together and then moving in.”

“If it was too fast—”

“I love you, Mydei. I’ve always loved you and I know you’ve waited long enough for this,” he continued. “I got so wrapped up in the little details like the perfect place, the perfect time,” he murmured. “but I think it’s always been here. Where it all began again.”

Mydei blinked, his posture shifting slightly as he caught the change in Phainon’s tone. 

Phainon stepped back, just enough to release his hand and then slowly dropped to one knee. His hand fumbled slightly in his pocket as he reached for the small velvet box. 

“Mydei,” he said softly. “Will you marry me?”

For a moment, Mydei didn’t speak and the world had slowed to that moment. 

He stared down at Phianon, lips parted slightly, the last rays of evening sun catching all the soft angles of his face in the most perfect way possible. His expression flickered through surprise and disbelief. 

“Are you serious?” he asked, voice breathy. 

Phainon gave a quiet laugh, holding the box up a little higher and nodded. 

Mydei’s hand fellow to his mouth, eyes welling up faster than he could control. “God, I—Phai—” he whispered. 

“Is that a yes?”

Mydei nodded, too choked up to speak. He pulled Phainon up to stand and kissed him firmly like it was the only answer he could give. Phainon melted into the kiss, one hand wrapping around Mydei’s waist as the other held onto the ring. 

“I love you,” Mydei whispered, pressing their foreheads together. “Of course it’s a yes.”

Phainon reached for the delicate ring. He slipped it onto Mydei’s finger and kissed his knuckles once, then the back of his palm. 

They were silent for a moment, breathing in the moment

“You’re going to have to tell Augusta that she gets to be a flower girl again," Mydei's voice cut through the silence. 

“Oh, she already knows,” Phainon responded, wrapping both arms around Mydei’s waist. 

Mydei laughed a little. “How did you manage that?”

Phainon let out a wistful sigh. “A lot of extra cookies.”

“Mmm,” Mydei hummed. “So that’s why she’s been bouncing off the walls lately.

“Forgive me?” 

“I’ll allow it,” he smiled softly, nudging his nose against Phainon's. Phainon pressed their lips together softly, letting Mydei’s fingers tangle into his coat as he melted into it. 

☼

The kitchen was alive with the soft clatter of utensils and the hiss of the pot on the stove. Augusta was in the living room, humming to herself as she danced around with Fig Stew in her arms. 

Phainon stood at the counter, slicing cherry tomatoes in half since Mydei had put him in charge of salad for dinner with Cas and Cipher. Mydei moved around the kitchen, checking the oven timer and adjusting the heat. Phainon liked nights like this—where everything felt easy and cozy. 

He glanced up and caught Mydei standing across the kitchen, staring down at his ring again. 

He set down the knife and wiped his hands on a towel, then crossed the short distance between them and slipped his arms around Mydei from behind, pressing his chest to Mydei’s back. 

“You keep looking at it,” Phainon said softly, nuzzling against the side of his neck. “If you don’t like it, we can switch it. I won’t be offended.”

Mydei scoffed, fingers absentmindedly brushing the ring as he leaned back into him. “I love it. It just…feels surreal.”

“Mm,” Phainon hummed, his arms tightening slightly.

“You’re clingy.”

“You said you missed it,” Phainon murmured, lips brushing his skin. “Trying to get my points back.”

Before Mydei could say anything, Augusta was making her way over to them with a wide grin on her face. “Mama, can I see it again?”

Mydei laughed and bent down to scoop her up into his arms, lifting her easily. He held out his hand to show off the ring. Augusta gasped, little hands covering her mouth. “It’s soo pretty and I can finally talk about it now!” she beamed. “I don’t have to keep it a secret anymore!”

“You were very sneaky, weren’t you?”

“I didn’t tell anyone,” Augusta said proudly. “Even when I wanted to tell everyone. Even Grandpa and Grandma.” 

“Well, we still have to keep it a secret from Auntie Cas and Cipher until dinner is over,” Phainon said, ruffling her hair. 

Augusta groaned just in time for the knock on the door to sound.

☼

Dinner had been full of conversation and Mydei had kept the ring well-hidden enough for even Cipher to not notice it—or if she had, she hadn’t mentioned it. 

They’d moved to the living room not too long after, the coffee table had been cleared to make room for hot tea and some select deserts courtesy of Mydei himself along with the charcuterie board that Castorice and Cipher had brought along with them. 

Augusta had been bouncing with excited energy all evening, and even Phainon could see her not-so-subtle glances at them. 

Phainon, curled up at one end of the couch beside Mydei, gave her a subtle nod, mouthing soon as he passed her another cracker with cheese on it. 

He cleared his throat, sharing a soft glance with Mydei. “There’s actually something we wanted to tell you tonight…” Phainon trailed off. 

Augusta gasped and sure enough—

“Mama and Papa are getting married!” she blurted out. 

Cipher nearly choked on her drink, coughing once and then grinning as she looked between them. “Wellllll, it’s about time, isn’t it?”

Castorice was on her feet from her spot on the rug, eyes wide as she crossed over to them. “This better not be a joke,” she said, already wiping a tear from her eye. 

Phainon threw a glance at Mydei. Mydei nodded once before pulling the ring from his pocket and slipping it back onto his finger. 

“This is beautiful,” she whispered

Cipher leaned over to take a look as well, lifting an eyebrow as she clapped Phainon on the back. 

“Ouu, not bad~” she smirked. “Who knew you had taste?”

Phainon rolled his eyes, but there was no malice behind it. 

Off to the side, Augusta stood with her shoulders curled in. Phainon noticed immediately and opened an arm for her. She hesitated for a second then shuffled forward, eyes not meeting his. 

“Sorry, Papa…” she murmured. “I ruined the surprise.”

“Hey, hey,” Phainon said softly, pulling her into his side and kissing her cheek. “I think it was perfect.”

Her mouth twitched, relief washing over her face. She giggled when Mydei reached over to tap her nose. 

"Even better this way," Mydei added.

That was when Cipher straightened, eyes narrowing in that exaggerated way of hers as she looked between the two of them with suspicion. 

“Ohhhh, little prince, “ she said to Mydei, grinning. “Don’t tell me you’ve got another one in there.”

Mydei blinked, heat rising to his cheeks. “What—no, I—I’m not pregnant,” he hissed. 

Phainon snorted. 

“We could change that,” Phainon replied without much thought, earning him a playful smack on the arm from his fiance.

“Phainon.”

“Pregnant?! Another baby?” Augusta’s eyes widened. “We’re finally getting another baby, Mama?!”

“No, no, sweetheart,” Mydei waved his hands. “There is no baby.”

Phainon glanced sideways at Mydei as he stood up. He muttered something to himself as he began clearing dishes. 

Castorice gathered a few empty teacups, laughing softly at the banter. “She’s just teasing, Mydei, but for what it’s worth—you two would be good at it,” she said, trailing after him. 

“Not you too!” Mydei called from the kitchen. 

Phainon smiled to himself. He hugged Augusta closer, tucking her head beneath his chin before dropping a kiss to the top of her head.

“No baby…” Augusta mumbled. 

“You won’t have to wait long, little one,” Cipher mused. 

“Cipher—” 

“Oh please,” she scoffed. “It’s a miracle you two don’t have another one by now with the way you look at him like you want to—”

Mydei cleared his throat loudly from the kitchen, and Phainon could feel his gaze burning into the back of his head. 

“Want to what?” Augusta asked curiously. 

“Okay!” Phainon announced as he stood with Augusta in his arms. “Bedtime for you, babygirl.”

“But I want to know too! Can’t I stay up a little longer.”

“Nope, not unless you want Papa to get in trouble,” he whispered. 

She gasped softly, clearly taking that very seriously.

And with that, he disappeared down the hall, his daughter nestled against his chest. 

☼

The lights were low and the bathroom fan hummed gently in the background from Mydei’s nighttime routine. Phainon had gotten Augusta to sleep without much protest, the boundless energy she’d had had finally fizzled out now that she didn’t have to hold in the secret. 

The sheets were pulled back in their bed and Phain sat against the headboard in an old shirt and boxers, scrolling idly through his phone while Mydei slipped beneath the covers beside him. 

Phainon held out an arm instinctively, letting Mydei’s head rest against his bicep. He set his phone down on the nightstand, then shifted to look at him. 

“You seemed surprised earlier,” he said softly, voice almost casual. “When Cipher brought up the baby thing.”

Mydei didn’t respond immediately. He glanced up at Phainon, throwing one arm around his middle. 

“I wasn’t expecting it to come up in front of everyone. That’s all.”

Phainon let a hand run through his hair, fingers smoothing along the back of his head. “But… you wouldn’t be… opposed?” 

Mydei playfully rolled his eyes, reaching a hand up to flick Phainon’s forehead with two fingers. “Don’t get ahead of yourself.”

“That didn’t sound like a no,” he teased. 

Mydei sighed in response, resting his forehead against Phainon’s chest. “We have a wedding to plan.” 

“Still not a no.”

“You’re insufferable,” he groaned, turning away from Phainon. Phainon frowned at the loss of contact.

Mydei wasn't really upset, was he? 

He shifted slightly, moving closer to Mydei until his chest was pressed against his bare back, arms wrapping around his waist, toying with the hem of his sweatpants. 

“Phainon…”

“Mydei…” Phainon dragged out the syllables. 

“I just want to focus on this first,” Mydei continued, turning onto his back as Phainon propped himself on one arm to look down at him. “You. Augusta. Actually getting married.”

A small smile tugged at Phainon’s lips. He leaned down to press a gentle kiss against Mydei’s lips. “Wedding first. Got it,” he said, dropping his weight onto Mydei, chin resting on his chest. 

“Then maybe,” Mydei brought a hand to his hair, threading gently, “we’ll see about the rest.”
